_comment: Semantic mapping for the supplied 48-tile stage tilesets. Shared by the
runtime (src/art/TilesetRegistry.ts) and the map generator
(tools/build-map.mjs).
TWO SEPARATE CONCERNS:
roles      - GAMEPLAY. Emitted onto the gameplay layers (collision, cover,
propCollision, shadowZones) and the only source of tile flags
the grid reads. Flags here are authoritative.
surfaces   - APPEARANCE ONLY. Per-area ground painting on the visual-only
`floor` layer. Changing a surface can never change walkability.
architecture - APPEARANCE ONLY. Wall faces, windows, doors and the roof
band drawn on the visual-only `architecture` layer.
MapLoader only merges tile flags from the gameplay layers, so a decorative
tile can never accidentally make a floor solid, and the same tile image may
appear in both a decorative and a gameplay role without its flags leaking.
Measured limitation driving the composition rules: only 28 of the 48 tiles
are visually distinct, and wall_solid / wall_variant / wall_left /
wall_right / wall_corner_tl / wall_corner_tr are near-identical art, so
there are no true directional wall edges to build corners from. See
docs/art-requests/phase-b1.md.

blocker.why: The single gameplay blocker for every non-walkable tile. The collision layer is invisible; what the player sees there is painted by the architecture layer, so appearance and collision cannot drift apart.

van.why: No van artwork exists in the package; the gameplay object keeps a generated placeholder sprite drawn over these tiles. See docs/art-integration.md.

_comment: variantChance is a percentage. It is kept low because the only available
floor variants are decorative motifs: at the previous 30% the market read
as patterned wallpaper rather than a village square.
floor_inlay and checker are deliberately NOT random variants - they are
framed motifs that only work as authored accents.
floor_stain is red blood spatter: deliberately unused in Valcendre, because
blood is an Abbey/Ascension escalation in the locked design, not village set
dressing.
Drawn outward from the playable area by Chebyshev distance to the nearest
walkable tile: a stone wall face, then a roof edge, then red roof tiles,
then darkness. That is what turns a flat ring of identical wall tiles into
buildings with pitched roofs, using only approved art.
wallSouth/wallNorth exist because wall_bottom and wall_top are the only
wall pieces measurably different from wall_solid.
grass/flowerbed/hedge are listed here as appearance-only names so garden
dressing can be drawn on decorBack, ABOVE the floor. The garden lane is an
authored shadow zone, so its floor must stay the dark concealment tile for
gameplay legibility; the greenery sits on top of it. The tileset has no
shaded-grass variant, which is requested in docs/art-requests/phase-b1.md.
